deliverable: Biostatistics input to the protocol: design rationale and design selection
description: The biostatistician's written justification of the overall design: randomization, blinding and placebo control, sequential cohorts and sentinel dosing for SAD and MAD, crossover versus parallel groups, and randomized versus fixed sequences for BE, BA, food-effect and DDI studies. It explains how the design answers the objectives and controls bias, including washout length relative to the expected half-life.
inputs: Development plan or target product profile; nonclinical PK and toxicology (NOAEL, exposure margins, predicted human PK and half-life); prior data on the compound or class; clinical pharmacology objectives; applicable guidance on first-in-human starting dose, early-trial risk mitigation and design-specific studies.
outputs: Design section of the protocol; basis for the estimands, sample-size rationale, randomization design, dose-escalation rules and SAP design assumptions.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E8(R1); Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); EMEA/CHMP/SWP/28367/07 Rev. 1; ICH M13A; ICH M12; Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs:…
qc: Independent biostatistician peer review; check of the design against objectives and estimands; medical, clinical pharmacology and regulatory review; protocol team agreement.

deliverable: Objectives, estimands and endpoints alignment (ICH E9(R1) estimand framework)
description: Maps each objective to a target estimand and its endpoints, defining the five attributes: treatment condition, population, variable (endpoint), intercurrent events with the strategy for each, and population-level summary. Many early-phase objectives are descriptive (PK parameters, safety), while comparative objectives (BE, food effect, DDI) estimate a geometric mean ratio with a confidence interval (90% for BE under ICH M13A); emesis, dosing errors, missed doses, prohibited medications and discontinuation each need an explicit strategy.
inputs: Protocol objectives; endpoint definitions; PK and PD variable list; anticipated intercurrent events (emesis, dosing errors, missed doses, rescue or concomitant medications, discontinuation); clinical input on the questions of interest.
outputs: Objectives and estimands section of the protocol; basis for analysis-set definitions, intercurrent-event handling rules in the SAP, and TLF planning.
standard: ICH E9(R1); Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); ICH M13A
qc: Independent biostatistician review of estimand completeness (all five attributes, every anticipated intercurrent event); clinical and clinical pharmacology review; consistency check of objectives, estimands, endpoints and analysis sets.

deliverable: Protocol statistical considerations section (analysis overview)
description: The protocol's statistical overview: analysis sets, planned analyses by domain (PK, PD, safety and comparative PK where applicable), descriptive-statistics conventions, summary-level handling of missing and BLQ data, interim or escalation decision references, and sample size. It states that full detail is in the SAP without pre-empting it.
inputs: Design rationale; estimand framework; analysis-set definitions; sample-size rationale; interim or adaptive elements; PK and PD analysis intent; safety review structure; the study's SOPs and protocol template.
outputs: Statistical considerations section of the protocol; the frame the SAP must operationalize; reference for the safety committee charter.
standard: Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); ICH E3
qc: Independent biostatistician peer review; alignment check against the estimands and the planned SAP scope; cross-functional protocol review.

deliverable: Analysis-set definitions (protocol level)
description: Defines each analysis set (for example enrolled, safety, PK concentration, PK parameter, PD, and the BE or comparison set in crossover studies) and the rules that move a participant or a profile in or out. Each estimand's population attribute is linked to a concrete set; the SAP later operationalizes the derivations.
inputs: Estimand population attributes; design structure (sentinel, cohort, crossover); PK exclusion criteria (emesis, dosing errors, missed samples, pre-dose concentrations); anticipated intercurrent events.
outputs: Analysis-sets subsection of the protocol; basis for ADSL population flags and the SAP analysis-set rules; population footnote for every TLF.
standard: ICH E9; Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); ICH M13A; ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Independent review of set definitions for mutual consistency and estimand linkage; clinical pharmacology review of PK exclusion rules; traceability check to the ADSL flag plan.

deliverable: Sample-size or precision justification (or documented rationale when there is no formal sizing, as in first-in-human cohorts)
description: For SAD and MAD cohorts, a documented rationale that cohort size is chosen for safety observation and PK characterization rather than power, with the precision expected for geometric-mean PK parameters. For comparative and special-population studies, the power or precision calculation is documented in the design module's design and sample-size basis (BE-01, BA-01, FE-01, DDI-01, QT-01, RI-01 or HI-01) and summarized here with the method and software version.
inputs: Design (crossover or parallel, cohort size, active-to-placebo ratio); within- and between-participant CV assumptions from prior or class data; assumed geometric mean ratio and acceptance limits for comparative studies; target probability of observing an adverse event of a given incidence; precision targets.
outputs: Sample-size subsection of the protocol; assumptions carried into the SAP; input to feasibility and enrollment planning.
standard: ICH E9; ICH M13A; Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); Statistical Approaches to Establishing Bioequivalence
qc: Independent recalculation with separate code or software; review of assumptions against their sources; method, software version and any seed recorded.

deliverable: Randomization design and specification (including sentinel dosing and active-to-placebo allocation)
description: Defines the allocation method (for example permuted blocks within cohort to keep the active-to-placebo ratio), stratification, the blinding scheme, the sentinel-dosing scheme for first-in-human cohorts, and sequence randomization for crossover studies, plus who generates and who holds the schedule. Details that make allocation predictable, such as block size, belong in the restricted randomization specification, not in the protocol.
inputs: Design (cohorts, sequences, sentinel scheme, ratio); blinding plan; IRT capabilities; dose-escalation structure; number of cohorts or periods; sample size.
outputs: Randomization and blinding text in the protocol; design inputs for the restricted randomization specification, IRT setup and the code-break plan.
standard: ICH E9; EMEA/CHMP/SWP/28367/07 Rev. 1; ICH M13A
qc: Independent biostatistician review; check that block, ratio and sentinel logic enforce the intended allocation; segregation of duties (the specification author does not generate the schedule); blinding-integrity review.

deliverable: Safety review committee or DMC charter: statistical decision rules and dose-escalation criteria
description: Biostatistics content of the safety review committee (or DMC) charter: the escalation algorithm (rule-based or model-based), the safety, tolerability and PK data reviewed before each escalation, stopping and de-escalation rules, exposure limits tied to nonclinical margins, and review cadence. It also defines data flow to the committee, blinded versus unblinded views, and the firewall.
inputs: Design and dose levels; nonclinical exposure margins and NOAEL; predicted human PK; stopping-rule approach; escalation method; operating-characteristics results when model-based; committee composition and governance; unblinding and firewall rules.
outputs: Statistical and escalation sections of the charter; specification of the data packages and summaries the committee receives at each review.
standard: EMEA/CHMP/SWP/28367/07 Rev. 1; Guidance for Clinical Trial Sponsors: Establishment and…; ICH E9
qc: Independent review of decision rules for clarity and conservatism; consistency check against protocol dose levels and stopping rules; committee and regulatory review; review of operating characteristics when the design is model-based.

deliverable: Dose-escalation operating-characteristics simulation (design stage)
description: Simulation of the chosen escalation design before the study starts. For rule-based designs it gives the probability of escalating or stopping under assumed dose-toxicity and dose-exposure scenarios; for model-based designs it gives the probability of selecting each dose, the risk of overdosing, expected sample size and sensitivity to the prior, with seeds, software versions and the scenario grid recorded.
inputs: Escalation rule or model and priors; dose levels and cohort sizes; assumed dose-toxicity and dose-exposure scenarios; target toxicity interval or escalation thresholds; nonclinical predictions.
outputs: Operating-characteristics tables and figures supporting the protocol design section and the committee charter.
standard: Adaptive Design Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biologics:…; EMEA/CHMP/SWP/28367/07 Rev. 1
qc: Independent re-run with the documented seed and environment; code review; review of the scenario grid for completeness; sanity check of results against design intuition.

deliverable: Interim and adaptive design elements specification (if any)
description: Specifies any adaptive features beyond simple sequential escalation, such as sample-size re-estimation, adaptive dose or cohort selection, optional cohorts triggered by emerging PK, or a two-stage BE design: decision points, methods, error-rate and operating-characteristic control, independence of the analysis, and information flow. When none are planned, it is a documented not-applicable statement.
inputs: Design objectives; escalation and interim structure; nonclinical and emerging-PK expectations; regulatory feedback on adaptation.
outputs: Adaptive-design subsection of the protocol and SAP; input to interim output specifications, the unblinding and firewall plan, and simulations.
standard: Adaptive Design Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biologics:…; ICH E9; Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP)
qc: Independent statistical review of adaptation rules and error-rate control; simulation of operating characteristics where needed; firewall and independence review; documented not-applicable decision when no adaptation is planned.

deliverable: PK precision and variability assumptions memo (CV, BLQ and LLOQ, sampling-schedule adequacy)
description: Supporting memo for the sample-size and PK rationale: assumed within- and between-participant CV for key PK parameters with their sources, the assay LLOQ and expected BLQ pattern, and an assessment that the sampling schedule characterizes Cmax, tmax, AUC and the terminal phase. For BE studies it checks the ICH M13A expectations that AUC(0-t) covers at least 80% of AUC(0-inf) and that sampling spans at least three terminal half-lives.
inputs: Predicted human PK (nonclinical, allometry or PBPK); assay LLOQ; literature or class CV; proposed sampling times; AUC extrapolation acceptance criteria.
outputs: Assumptions for the sample-size rationale and the SAP NCA and BLQ rules; justification of the sampling schedule in the protocol; input to ADPC and ADPP planning.
standard: ICH M13A; Bioavailability Studies Submitted in NDAs or INDs:…
qc: Joint biostatistician and PK scientist review; check of sampling adequacy against the predicted half-life; sensitivity of precision to the CV assumptions; source of every assumption documented.

deliverable: Biostatistics protocol review and sign-off
description: Documented biostatistics review and approval of the final protocol and each amendment: internal consistency of objectives, estimands, endpoints, analysis sets and planned analyses, and correctness of the sample-size, randomization, blinding and escalation text. It is captured as tracked comments with resolutions and a signature in the protocol approval record.
inputs: Final draft protocol and amendments; estimand framework; sample-size and randomization specifications; committee charter; the study's protocol-approval SOP.
outputs: Signed biostatistics approval record; comment-resolution log; clearance for protocol finalization and the start of SAP and specification work.
standard: ICH E9; Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Comment tracking and resolution log; second-biostatistician consistency check of objectives, estimands and endpoints; signed, audit-trailed approval; amendment version control.

deliverable: Emergency unblinding and code-break plan (design-stage definition)
description: Protocol- and charter-level definition of the emergency-unblinding pathway and the blinding firewall: who may unblind and when, the IRT mechanism, which unblinded roles (committee, PK or safety reviewers, expedited safety reporting) work behind a controlled barrier, and how unblinding events are logged and reported. It sets the governance that later code-break execution must follow.
inputs: Blinding scheme and randomization design; committee firewall needs; IRT capabilities; expedited safety-reporting requirements; the study's unblinding SOP.
outputs: Unblinding and firewall section of the protocol and committee charter; requirements for the operational code-break plan and the unblinding event log.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R3); 21 CFR Part 312
qc: Independent review of the firewall and segregation of duties; check that the pathway is auditable and minimally disruptive to the blind; cross-check against the charter and randomization design.

deliverable: Blinded sample-size re-estimation (BSSR) plan: design-stage provision
description: Prespecified provision for blinded sample-size re-estimation, for example re-estimating within-participant PK variability or a PD variance from pooled blinded data. It defines the trigger, who performs it, what is recomputed, the maximum sample size, and how blinding and the type 1 error are protected; it is separate from the initial sample-size justification.
inputs: Protocol design; PK and PD variability assumptions memo; estimand definitions; initial sample-size calculation.
outputs: Re-estimation section in the protocol or SAP; reference to the procedure that keeps the data blinded.
standard: ICH E9; Adaptive Design Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biologics:…
qc: Biostatistician review and sign-off; confirmation that only blinded data are used; documented calculation.

deliverable: Estimand-to-design traceability and assumptions log (intercurrent-event strategy register)
description: A register that records, for each estimand, the five attributes, the strategy for each intercurrent event with its rationale and assumptions, and the design element and analysis set that implement it. It is kept current through amendments and carried into the SAP.
inputs: Protocol objectives; estimand definitions; endpoint definitions; analysis-set definitions.
outputs: Estimand attribute table with intercurrent-event strategies, rationale and assumptions; reference for the SAP estimand and analysis-set sections.
standard: ICH E9(R1)
qc: Biostatistician and medical reviewer sign-off; check that every intercurrent event in the protocol has a strategy and an implementing rule.

deliverable: Statistics input to critical-to-quality factors and quality tolerance limits
description: Statistics contribution to the study's quality-by-design work: names the data and processes critical to the primary estimands (for example dosing and sampling clock times, pre-dose samples, emesis and meal timing, ECG timing) and proposes trial-level acceptable ranges where useful, so that monitoring, edit checks and QC focus on them.
inputs: Objectives and estimands; design and analysis overview; known risks of the design (for example carryover, emesis, sampling-time deviations).
outputs: List of critical data and processes with proposed acceptable ranges; input to the risk assessment, monitoring and data management plans, edit checks and risk-based QC tiering.
standard: ICH E6(R3); ICH E8(R1)
qc: Cross-functional review; each critical item mapped to a control (edit check, monitoring step or QC level).

deliverable: Relative bioavailability or formulation-bridging design and precision basis
description: Protocol statistics for a study comparing formulations, or a formulation with an intravenous or oral solution reference: whether the objective is to estimate relative bioavailability or to bridge formulations against predefined confidence-interval limits, the design (crossover, parallel for a long half-life, extra periods for several formulations), the reference, dose normalization when strengths differ, and a precision- or power-based sample size.
inputs: Formulation development plan; prior PK and variability; intended use of the results (dose selection, bridging a clinical formulation to the to-be-marketed one); half-life.
outputs: Protocol objectives, design and sample-size sections; inputs to the BA analysis section of the SAP and the randomization specification.
standard: Bioavailability Studies Submitted in NDAs or INDs:…; ICH M13A
qc: Independent review of objective, decision criteria and sample-size calculation against the development plan.

deliverable: BE design and sample-size basis (2x2, replicate or parallel)
description: Protocol statistics for a bioequivalence study: a randomized single-dose crossover, a partial or full replicate crossover for a highly variable drug, or a parallel design for a long half-life, with washout and fasting or fed conditions. The sample size is calculated for the chosen design and analysis, with the assumed GMR, within-participant CV, power, dropout allowance and sensitivity to the assumptions stated.
inputs: Within-participant CV and GMR from earlier studies or literature; half-life; comparator and strength; fasting or fed requirement; planned analysis (average or reference-scaled BE).
outputs: Protocol design and sample-size sections; sequences for the randomization specification; inputs to the BE analysis section of the SAP.
standard: ICH M13A; Statistical Approaches to Establishing Bioequivalence
qc: Independent re-calculation of the sample size with the stated software and assumptions; check that design, sequences and planned analysis agree.

deliverable: Drug interaction study design and sample-size basis
description: Protocol statistics for a clinical drug interaction study: the investigational drug's role (object or precipitant), a one-sequence or randomized crossover (preferred) or a parallel design for long half-lives, the precipitant's dose, duration and timing (for example multiple-dose pretreatment for inducers), substrate dosing, and a sample size giving a reliable estimate of the size and variability of the interaction.
inputs: In vitro and PBPK predictions; precipitant and substrate PK (half-lives, time to steady state, enzyme turnover); within-participant variability; safety of combined dosing.
outputs: Protocol design, dosing schedule and sample-size sections; inputs to the DDI analysis section.
standard: ICH M12
qc: Independent review of the dosing schedule against precipitant and substrate PK; sample-size rationale re-derived.

deliverable: Food-effect design and sample-size basis
description: Protocol statistics for a food-effect study: randomized, balanced, single-dose, two-period crossover of fed versus fasted (three periods when two formulations are compared), washout, a parallel design for a long half-life, the test meal, the dose, and a sample size that characterizes the food effect given PK variability. It separates a pilot assessment (for example within first-in-human) from the definitive study with the to-be-marketed formulation.
inputs: Formulation status (clinical or to-be-marketed); PK variability and half-life; tolerability of a high-fat meal; safety of the planned dose.
outputs: Protocol design, meal specification and sample-size sections; inputs to the randomization specification and the food-effect analysis section.
standard: Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs:…; CPMP/EWP/560/95/Rev. 1 Corr. 2**
qc: Independent review of design, meal composition and sample-size rationale against the guidance.

deliverable: Hepatic impairment design and sample-size basis
description: Protocol statistics for a hepatic impairment PK study: mild, moderate and severe groups by Child-Pugh class, or a staged design that starts with one impairment group; a within-study control group matched on factors that affect PK; stability requirements before dosing; unbound sampling for highly bound drugs; and a precision-based sample size per group.
inputs: Hepatic elimination and protein binding; expected population and liver disease etiology; prior variability; safety of dosing in severe impairment.
outputs: Protocol design, classification, matching and sample-size sections; inputs to the hepatic analysis section and enrollment tracking.
standard: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic…; CPMP/EWP/2339/02
qc: Independent review of classification, staging rule, matching and sample-size calculation.

deliverable: Cardiac safety (QT) design and sample-size basis
description: Protocol statistics for QT assessment: a thorough QT study (randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled, with a positive control for assay sensitivity, crossover or parallel) or a concentration-QTc analysis of first-in-human or MAD data with doses giving exposures well above the high clinical exposure. Either way it fixes replicate baseline ECGs, ECG times matched to PK samples around Cmax, and a sample-size or precision rationale.
inputs: Predicted therapeutic and high clinical exposures (including interaction and organ-impairment scenarios); nonclinical QT findings; PK profile and half-life; dose limits for safety.
outputs: Protocol ECG schedule, dose plan, positive-control decision and sample-size sections; inputs to the cardiodynamic analysis plan and the ECG core-laboratory specification.
standard: ICH E14; ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1)
qc: Independent review of exposure coverage and the ECG schedule; sample-size or precision calculation re-derived.

deliverable: Renal impairment design and sample-size basis
description: Protocol statistics for a renal impairment PK study: a full design across renal function groups, or a reduced worst-case design (severe impairment versus control) with a staged expansion rule; one renal function method for enrollment; a control group matched on factors that affect PK; dialysis periods if needed; and a precision-based sample size per group.
inputs: Fraction excreted renally and elimination pathways; predicted exposure change; expected population and dialysis use; prior PK variability.
outputs: Protocol design, group definitions, matching criteria and sample-size sections; inputs to the renal analysis section and enrollment tracking.
standard: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal…; Guideline on the evaluation of the pharmacokinetics of…
qc: Independent review of group definitions, matching and sample-size calculation; enrollment method checked against the planned analysis.

deliverable: Statistical analysis plan (SAP)
description: The signed plan that operationalizes the protocol: estimands, analysis sets, all PK, PD and safety methods, any inferential models (BE, food-effect, DDI, concentration-QTc), missing-data and intercurrent-event handling, multiplicity, BLQ rules cross-referenced to the PK analysis plan, and the planned outputs. It is finalized before database lock and unblinding.
inputs: Final protocol and amendments; estimand framework; committee charter; regulatory feedback; scope of ADaM and TLF work.
outputs: Authoritative source for analysis-set rules, ADaM and programming specifications, TLF shells and Stage 4 analyses; CSR Appendix 16.1.9.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); ICH E3; ICH M13A
qc: Senior biostatistician peer review; cross-check against the protocol and estimands; documented sign-off; version control of all amendments.

deliverable: SAP amendment and version-control log
description: Change-control record for every SAP revision: what changed (estimands, methods, analysis sets, TLF scope), why, who approved it, and when each change was made relative to the blind review and unblinding. Changes made after unblinding are flagged so the CSR can describe them.
inputs: Prior SAP versions; protocol amendments; committee or regulatory input; change requests; blind review outcomes.
outputs: Audit trail for CSR Section 9.8 and Appendix 16.1.9; evidence that the primary analyses were prespecified.
standard: ICH E3; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Independent review of each change; change dates checked against lock and unblinding dates; audit trail retained.

deliverable: Analysis-set definitions and derivation rules (SAP level)
description: Precise, programmable rules for each analysis set (for example enrolled, randomized, safety, PK concentration, PK parameter, PD, per-protocol or completers, and BE, food-effect or DDI comparison sets), including profile-level PK exclusions and who decides them and when, normally at the blind review.
inputs: Protocol analysis sets; SAP; estimand intercurrent-event handling; PK exclusion rules.
outputs: ADSL population flags and their derivation rules; denominators for every TLF; decision list for the blind review.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; ICH E9; ICH M13A
qc: Independent reviewer confirms flag logic against the SAP; flags double-programmed in ADSL; set membership reconciled at the blind review.

deliverable: TLF shells (tables, listings and figures)
description: Mock shells for every planned table, listing and figure with final titles, column headers, row structure, population footnotes, decimal conventions, programmer notes and placeholder values. Coverage spans disposition, demographics, exposure, deviations, PK concentrations and mean profiles (linear and semi-log), NCA parameters, dose proportionality, comparative PK, concentration-QTc, safety, PD, immunogenicity and listings.
inputs: SAP; PK analysis plan; TLF inventory; analysis-set definitions; the study's output conventions.
outputs: Programming target for Stage 4 TLF production; basis for medical-writing review of CSR tables.
standard: ICH E3; ICH M13A
qc: Peer, medical-writer and clinical review; titles and footnotes checked against the SAP; layout tested with dummy data.

deliverable: TLF inventory (table of contents)
description: Master numbered index of all tables, listings and figures with output number, title, analysis set and SAP cross-reference, marking in-text versus appendix placement and the CSR section each output supports. It drives scope, production tracking and QC completeness checks.
inputs: SAP; analysis-set definitions; ICH E3 report structure.
outputs: Production tracking list; CSR section mapping; QC completeness ledger.
standard: ICH E3
qc: Cross-check against SAP analyses (no orphan or missing outputs); peer review.

deliverable: ADaM specification: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis Dataset)
description: Specification of the one-record-per-participant dataset: population flags, planned and actual treatment variables (TRTxxP, TRTxxA), reference dates (for example TRTSDT), demographics, baseline characteristics, disposition and stratification, each with its derivation and metadata. Every other ADaM dataset merges from it.
inputs: SAP; analysis-set definitions; SDTM mapping for DM, EX, DS and SV; controlled terminology.
outputs: ADSL dataset (Stage 3); merge source for all ADaM datasets; population denominators.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; Define-XML v2.1; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Specification peer review; independent double programming of ADSL; CDISC conformance checks.

deliverable: ADaM specification: ADPC (PK concentrations)
description: BDS specification for PK concentration analysis data: nominal and actual relative times (NFRLT and AFRLT from first dose, NRRLT and ARRLT from the reference dose), analyte, concentration and units, BLQ and LLOQ flags and handling rules, profile and record exclusion flags, and pre-dose handling. It is the analysis-ready bridge from SDTM PC and EX to the NCA input.
inputs: SAP and PK analysis plan (BLQ, time and exclusion rules); SDTM PC and EX mapping; bioanalytical LLOQ; ADSL specification.
outputs: ADPC dataset (Stage 3); NCA input; concentration tables and figures.
standard: ADNCA v1.0; ADaMIG v1.3; ICH M13A
qc: Specification review against the PK analysis plan (BLQ and time rules); independent double programming of ADPC; reconciliation to SDTM PC.

deliverable: ADaM specification: ADPP (PK parameters)
description: BDS specification for NCA parameters carried into analysis (for example Cmax, tmax, AUC(0-t), AUC(0-inf), half-life, CL/F, Vz/F, percent AUC extrapolated, lambda-z and accumulation ratios): parameter codes and terminology, units, dose, period and treatment structure, and the rules that link validated NCA output to the dataset. Reported values come from the validated NCA software, not from re-derivation in the dataset program.
inputs: SAP and PK analysis plan (parameter list and acceptance rules); ADPC specification; structure of the NCA output; ADSL specification.
outputs: ADPP dataset; NCA summary tables, dose-proportionality, comparative PK and exposure-response inputs.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH M13A
qc: Specification review against the parameter list; ADPP reconciled to validated NCA output; independent double programming of the structure.

deliverable: ADaM specification: ADAE (adverse events)
description: Occurrence data structure specification for adverse events: MedDRA SOC and PT, treatment-emergent flag derivation relative to dosing (and to each period in crossover studies), severity, relationship and seriousness, and occurrence flags for first-occurrence summaries.
inputs: SAP; SDTM AE mapping; MedDRA version; ADSL specification; exposure data.
outputs: ADAE dataset; TEAE, SAE and death tables; AE listings.
standard: ADaM OCCDS v1.1; MedDRA Version 29.1; Define-XML v2.1
qc: Specification review of treatment-emergent logic; independent double programming; reconciliation to SDTM AE.

deliverable: ADaM specifications: ADLB, ADVS and ADEG (laboratory, vital signs, ECG)
description: BDS specifications for safety laboratory (chemistry, hematology, urinalysis), vital signs and ECG data: baseline and change from baseline, analysis visits and windows, standardized units, reference ranges, abnormality and toxicity-grade flags, and for ECG the heart-rate-corrected QT variables and categorical outlier flags.
inputs: SAP; SDTM LB, VS and EG mapping; controlled terminology; reference ranges and toxicity grading scale; QT correction method from the protocol or SAP.
outputs: ADLB, ADVS and ADEG datasets; safety summary and shift tables; concentration-QTc input.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; ICH E14; CTCAE v6.0 (MedDRA 28.0); Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation
qc: Specification review of baseline, window and unit logic; independent double programming; reconciliation to SDTM.

deliverable: ADaM specification: ADPD (pharmacodynamics)
description: BDS specification for PD and biomarker endpoints: parameter definitions, baseline, change and percent change, analysis windows, and the keys that link PD records to time-matched concentrations for PK/PD analysis.
inputs: SAP or PD analysis plan; SDTM PD or biomarker mapping; ADSL and ADPC specifications.
outputs: ADPD dataset; PD tables and figures; exposure-response inputs.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; Define-XML v2.1
qc: Specification review against the PD plan; independent double programming; reconciliation to SDTM.

deliverable: SDTM mapping specification
description: Source-to-SDTM mapping that defines how each CRF field and external transfer maps to SDTM domains and variables (for example DM, EX, PC, PP, AE, LB, VS, EG, DS, MH, CM, DV), including controlled-terminology assignments, derivations, --SEQ and RELREC linkage, and supplemental qualifiers. It drives the SDTM build and the annotated CRF.
inputs: Final CRF and EDC structure; SDTMIG; controlled terminology plan; protocol; data-transfer specifications.
outputs: SDTM datasets (Stage 3); annotated CRF; SDTM Define-XML metadata.
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology; Define-XML v2.1
qc: Independent review against SDTMIG and controlled terminology; conformance rule check; raw-to-SDTM traceability check.

deliverable: Annotated CRF (aCRF): preparation and review
description: The blank CRF annotated with SDTM domains and variables, the human-readable link between collected data and SDTM. It is prepared and reviewed against the final CRF and the mapping specification and is expected in a standardized-data submission.
inputs: Final blank CRF; SDTM mapping specification; SDTMIG and controlled terminology.
outputs: Submission aCRF; origin metadata for Define-XML; input to the SDTM reviewer guide.
standard: Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…; SDTMIG v3.4
qc: Page-by-page review against the mapping specification; consistency with Define-XML origins; peer review.

deliverable: Programming and derivation specifications
description: Programmer-facing specifications behind ADaM datasets and TLFs: algorithmic derivation logic, variable- and value-level metadata, formats and lengths, and explicit rules for complex derivations such as windowing, baseline, treatment emergence, BLQ handling and dose normalization.
inputs: SAP; ADaM specifications; SDTM mapping; TLF shells; controlled terminology.
outputs: Targets for production and independent QC programming in Stages 3 and 4.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; Define-XML v2.1
qc: Independent specification review; basis for double-programming reconciliation; traceability to the SAP.

deliverable: PK analysis plan (NCA detail)
description: Detailed non-compartmental analysis specification, standalone or as an SAP appendix: full parameter list, BLQ handling by position in the profile, nominal versus actual time rules, lambda-z selection and acceptance criteria, profile and parameter exclusion rules, the AUC calculation method, and the validated NCA software and settings.
inputs: Protocol PK schedule; SAP; bioanalytical LLOQ; sampling-time conventions; PK precision memo.
outputs: ADPC and ADPP specifications; NCA setup; PK concentration and parameter tables.
standard: ICH M13A; Bioavailability Studies Submitted in NDAs or INDs:…
qc: PK scientist and biostatistician review; rules cross-checked against the SAP; NCA software settings and templates qualified.

deliverable: Population PK and exposure-response modeling analysis plan (PMAP)
description: Separate modeling plan for population PK and exposure-response: objectives, data and BLQ handling for modeling, structural, statistical and covariate model building, estimation methods, model evaluation (goodness of fit, visual predictive checks, bootstrap), simulation objectives and reporting. It is written before modeling starts.
inputs: Protocol objectives and sampling design; SAP; PK and PD scope; prior models and literature.
outputs: Modeling run plan; modeling dataset specification; pharmacometrics report (Stage 4); dosing recommendations.
standard: Population Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Industry; Exposure-Response Relationships: Study Design, Data…; CHMP/EWP/185990/06; ICH M15
qc: Independent pharmacometrics review; model-evaluation criteria prespecified; run records reproducible.

deliverable: PK/PD modeling dataset specification
description: Specification for the modeling-ready dataset: dose and observation event records (for example EVID, MDV, AMT, RATE, DV and time), covariates, BLQ handling for modeling, units, and traceability to ADPC, ADSL and exposure data.
inputs: Modeling analysis plan; ADPC, ADSL and exposure data; PD data when exposure-response is in scope.
outputs: Modeling dataset; dataset appendix to the pharmacometrics report.
standard: ADaM popPK IG v1.0; Population Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Industry
qc: Independent check against the ADaM sources; structure and covariate completeness verified; reproducible build.

deliverable: Randomization schedule generation
description: Generation of the validated, reproducible randomization schedule, including any sentinel, cohort or sequence allocation: block and stratification structure per the specification, documented seed and software, restricted storage, and transfer to the IRT. In blinded studies it is produced under access control by a statistician outside the blinded study team.
inputs: Randomization specification (ratio, blocks, strata, sentinel and cohort rules); validated generation software; documented seed.
outputs: Randomization list for the IRT and drug supply; treatment-assignment source for ADSL; CSR Appendix 16.1.7.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E3; ICH M13A; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Independent QC of the allocation against the specification (ratios, blocks, strata); seed and reproducibility verified; secured storage.

deliverable: Randomization specification (restricted, pre-generation)
description: Restricted specification written before generation: allocation ratio, block sizes, stratification, sentinel and cohort handling, IRT configuration requirements, and reproducibility (software, seed management). It is the controlled basis for schedule generation and IRT user acceptance testing.
inputs: Final protocol randomization design; dose-escalation rules; drug-supply constraints.
outputs: Instructions for schedule generation; IRT setup and user acceptance testing; ADSL treatment derivation logic.
standard: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Independent review against the protocol; alignment with IRT user acceptance testing; documented approval.

deliverable: Unblinding and code-break plan
description: Operational plan for planned unblinding after database lock and for emergency code-breaks: who may unblind and when, the lock-then-unblind sequence, how the blind is kept for analysis programming, firewall roles, the emergency procedure and its log, and committee access.
inputs: Protocol and design-stage unblinding provisions; committee charter; randomization specification; the study's SOPs.
outputs: Controlled unblinding at lock (Stage 4); unblinding event log; firewall definition for analysis.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E2A; ICH E6(R3)
qc: Alignment review against SOPs and the charter; role and firewall verification; emergency-unblinding procedure and log tested.

deliverable: Data review plan (blinded data review)
description: Plan for the blind review of cleaned data before lock and unblinding: listings and summaries to produce, data-quality and protocol-deviation checks, PK profile and sample review, criteria and decision authority for analysis-set and PK exclusions, and how meeting decisions are documented.
inputs: SAP; analysis-set definitions; PK exclusion rules; protocol-deviation conventions; data management plan.
outputs: Blind review outputs and meeting (Stage 3); documented exclusion and analysis-set decisions before unblinding.
standard: ICH E9; ICH M13A
qc: Peer review; decisions recorded with timestamps before unblinding; consistency with the SAP.

deliverable: Define-XML planning and metadata strategy
description: Up-front plan for SDTM and ADaM Define-XML: dataset, variable and value-level metadata conventions, how origins and derivations are documented, controlled-terminology references and computational methods, built into the mapping and ADaM specifications so define.xml is produced by design rather than retrofitted.
inputs: Controlled terminology plan; Define-XML version; the study's metadata conventions; submission plans.
outputs: Metadata conventions applied in the SDTM mapping and ADaM specifications; SDTM and ADaM Define-XML (Stage 3); reviewer guide content.
standard: Define-XML v2.1; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…
qc: Metadata completeness against the specifications; Define-XML checks; value-level metadata review.

deliverable: Controlled terminology plan and dictionary version pinning
description: Records which CDISC Controlled Terminology, MedDRA and WHODrug versions the study uses, how sponsor-defined or extensible terms are handled, and when versions may change, pinned at planning for reproducibility and conformance across SDTM and ADaM.
inputs: SDTMIG and ADaMIG versions; CDISC Controlled Terminology releases; MedDRA and WHODrug versions; mapping conventions.
outputs: Terminology applied in SDTM and ADaM; Define-XML codelist references; reviewer guide notes.
standard: CDISC Controlled Terminology; MedDRA Version 29.1; WHODrug Global (UMCDD)
qc: Version-pin verification; terminology conformance checks; review of extensible codelist values.

deliverable: Validation and QC plan (independent double-programming strategy)
description: Risk-based plan that assigns a QC method to each ADaM dataset and TLF (independent double programming, independent review or code review), defines reconciliation and discrepancy logging, and sets software and environment qualification expectations. It requires every reported number, including NCA results, to come from a validated program with the software and version recorded.
inputs: SAP; TLF inventory; dataset list; risk assessment; the study's SOPs.
outputs: Stage 4 QC execution; reconciliation and discrepancy logs; validation records for the CSR and inspection.
standard: ICH E9; ICH E6(R3)
qc: QC-level assignments reviewed and approved; double programming mandatory for key outputs; plan kept audit-ready.

deliverable: Dummy data for shell and program testing
description: Synthetic datasets that follow the planned ADaM structures, used to test TLF shells, exercise programming specifications and dry-run derivations before real data arrive, without touching participant data.
inputs: ADaM and programming specifications; TLF shells; CDISC structures.
outputs: Shell renders and dry-run outputs; specification defect findings; production code ready before lock.
standard: ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Structure conformance to the ADaM specifications; coverage of edge cases (BLQ values, missing data, window boundaries).

deliverable: Data-transfer specifications (external data interface review)
description: Biostatistics and programming input to transfer agreements for external data (for example central laboratory, ECG core laboratory, bioanalytical concentrations, biomarkers): file structure, units, LLOQ and BLQ conventions, identifiers and keys, transfer frequency and reconciliation approach, so vendor data load cleanly into SDTM.
inputs: Vendor agreements; CRF and data management plan; laboratory and bioanalytical specifications; SDTM targets.
outputs: Agreed transfer specifications; clean loads into SDTM PC, LB and EG; reconciliation basis for Stage 3.
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; ICH E6(R3)
qc: Test-transfer review; key, format and unit verification; reconciliation procedure agreed.

deliverable: Dose-escalation and operating-characteristics simulation plan and outputs
description: Planning-stage simulation specification with archived, reproducible code that characterizes operating characteristics where needed (dose-escalation rules, CV-driven precision or sample size, adaptive elements), supporting the committee's decision rules and the protocol's statistical justification. It is re-run when amendments change the rules.
inputs: Final protocol design and escalation rules; assumed PK and CV; prior data; design-stage operating-characteristics results.
outputs: Operating-characteristics summaries supporting the committee rules and the SAP or protocol justification; archived code and seeds.
standard: Adaptive Design Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biologics:…; ICH E9
qc: Independent review of assumptions and code; seeds and environment documented; results sanity-checked.

deliverable: Interim analysis plan: committee statistical output specifications and firewall
description: Operational specification of interim or committee outputs: the exact tables and listings, data cutoff and snapshot procedure, any formal stopping boundaries, the split between open and closed session outputs, and the statistical firewall that keeps the independent statistician separate from the blinded study team.
inputs: Committee charter; escalation rules; unblinding and firewall plan.
outputs: Interim output specifications and shells; firewall procedure; committee output packages.
standard: ICH E9; Guidance for Clinical Trial Sponsors: Establishment and…
qc: Independent statistician produces outputs from documented snapshots; firewall access reviewed; outputs reproducible from archived code.

deliverable: Bioanalytical data-transfer and PK sample reconciliation specification
description: Dedicated transfer specification for the bioanalytical laboratory feed: concentration results and units, LLOQ and BLQ conventions, analytical run metadata, links from sample identifiers to collection times and nominal time points, and handling of reanalysis and incurred-sample reanalysis results, with rules for reconciling collected, shipped and assayed samples.
inputs: Bioanalytical laboratory data dictionary; sampling schedule; LLOQ definition; sample-handling manual.
outputs: Bioanalytical transfer specification; sample reconciliation rules; BLQ and LLOQ handling conventions.
standard: ICH M10; SDTMIG v3.4; ICH M13A
qc: Double check against the laboratory data dictionary; PK scientist sign-off.

deliverable: Value-level metadata (VLM) specification for Define-XML
description: Value-level metadata for parameter-based data: where-clauses, origins, derivations, codelists and computational methods for each PARAMCD in ADPC, ADPP, ADLB, ADVS, ADEG and ADPD, and for each test code in SDTM PC and PP, as Define-XML requires.
inputs: ADaM and SDTM specifications; controlled terminology; derivation specifications.
outputs: Value-level metadata tables that feed define.xml.
standard: Define-XML v2.1; ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Independent review against the datasets; Define-XML validation.

deliverable: Software and computing environment validation and qualification records
description: Evidence of the validated state of the analysis software and computing environment: installation and operational qualification records, versions of statistical, NCA, modeling and conformance software, change control, and a validated-environment attestation for the study.
inputs: Software inventory; vendor qualification documents; environment configuration; validation and QC plan.
outputs: Software validation summary; version register; validated-environment attestation.
standard: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd Edition; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R3); EMA/INS/GCP/112288/2023
qc: QA review; reported numbers produced only in qualified environments.

deliverable: IRT user acceptance testing: randomization and cohort-assignment scripts and sign-off
description: Biostatistics test scripts, run in the IRT test environment with a dummy schedule, confirming that the system allocates as the randomization specification requires (ratio, blocks, strata, sentinel and cohort sequencing, dose-level assignment), handles emergency unblinding and passes assignments to EDC correctly. Includes the defect log and the go-live sign-off.
inputs: Randomization specification; IRT requirements and configuration; dummy randomization schedule; sentinel and dose-escalation rules.
outputs: Executed test scripts, requirement-to-test traceability, defect log with retests and signed go-live approval, filed as system validation records.
standard: ICH E6(R3); 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Second tester or reviewer for critical scripts; sign-off only when all critical tests pass and no critical or major defect is open.

deliverable: eCRF design review for analysis-critical data
description: Documented biostatistics review of the eCRF before the EDC build, confirming that every item the analysis needs is collected with the right precision and structure (for example actual clock times of dosing, PK samples and ECGs, emesis and meal times, reasons for missed samples), using standard collection structures that trace to SDTM.
inputs: Draft eCRF and completion guidelines; protocol schedule of activities; statistical considerations and analysis sets; critical-data list.
outputs: Review comments and sign-off; inputs to the SDTM mapping specification and the annotated CRF.
standard: ICH E6(R3); Clinical Data Acquisition Standards Harmonization…
qc: Comments tracked to resolution; final eCRF checked against the analysis data needs before go-live.

deliverable: BA analysis section: comparisons, reference and data-removal rules
description: Design-specific SAP section listing each test-versus-reference comparison, the model and whether each comparison uses all treatments or only the two compared, log-transformed exposure measures with GMRs and 90% CIs, absolute bioavailability from dose-normalized AUC when an intravenous reference is used, and the rules for pre-dose concentrations, emesis and outliers.
inputs: BA design basis; protocol estimands; formulations and strengths; NCA conventions.
outputs: SAP BA section; specifications for BA analysis flags and outputs.
standard: Bioavailability Studies Submitted in NDAs or INDs:…; Statistical Approaches to Establishing Bioequivalence
qc: Independent statistician review; each comparison mapped to an objective and an output.

deliverable: BE analysis section: model, acceptance limits and data-removal rules
description: Design-specific SAP section: primary parameters (Cmax and AUC(0-t), or AUC(0-72h) for long half-lives), log-transformed analysis by a prespecified GLM or mixed model (typically with sequence, participant within sequence, period and formulation), and the 90% CI of the test/reference GMR judged against 80.00% to 125.00%. It lists every prespecified reason for removing data and when each is documented.
inputs: Protocol design and estimand; BE design and sample-size basis; protocol data-removal criteria; NCA conventions (BLQ handling, actual times).
outputs: SAP BE section; specification for BE analysis-set flags and BE outputs; methods text for the CSR.
standard: ICH M13A; ICH M13A Guideline: Bioequivalence for Immediate-Release…; Statistical Approaches to Establishing Bioequivalence
qc: Independent statistician review against M13A; check that each removal rule is prespecified and has a documentation point before bioanalysis.

deliverable: Drug interaction analysis section: no-effect boundaries and model
description: Design-specific SAP section: GMR of object exposure (AUC, Cmax and, when applicable, Cmin) with versus without the precipitant, its 90% CI from a model suited to the design, prespecified no-effect boundaries (preferably based on exposure-response), handling of dropouts and incomplete profiles, and summaries of metabolites and precipitant concentrations where collected.
inputs: DDI design basis; exposure-response information for the object drug; protocol estimands.
outputs: SAP DDI section; specifications for treatment-condition derivations and DDI outputs.
standard: ICH M12
qc: Independent statistician review; boundaries justified and the model matched to the design.

deliverable: Food-effect analysis section
description: Design-specific SAP section: log-transformed AUC(0-inf), AUC(0-t) and Cmax compared fed versus fasted with the fasted condition as reference, the 90% CI of the GMR, the no-effect criterion (80% to 125% unless exposure-response supports other limits), descriptive comparison of Tmax and Tlag, and rules for periods where meal or fasting conditions were not met.
inputs: Food-effect design basis; protocol estimands; meal and fasting rules; exposure-response information.
outputs: SAP food-effect section; specifications for condition-compliance flags and food-effect outputs.
standard: Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs:…
qc: Independent statistician review; criterion, reference condition and compliance rules checked for ambiguity.

deliverable: Hepatic impairment analysis section
description: Design-specific SAP section: GMRs of total and unbound AUC and Cmax for each impairment group versus control with 90% CIs, regression on continuous components of the classification and other markers, dose normalization if doses differ, the staged-design decision rule, and the method for dose recommendations.
inputs: Hepatic design basis; protocol estimands; exposure-response information.
outputs: SAP hepatic section; specifications for classification derivations and outputs.
standard: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic…; CPMP/EWP/2339/02
qc: Independent statistician review.

deliverable: Cardiodynamic (concentration-QTc) analysis plan
description: Prespecified plan for the QT analysis: heart-rate correction, baseline and placebo adjustment, the concentration-QTc model and its components, model-selection criteria, checks for hysteresis and goodness of fit, the decision rule at the highest clinically relevant exposure, categorical analyses and the handling of pooled studies.
inputs: QT design basis; ECG core-laboratory methods; PK sampling schedule; definitions of therapeutic and high clinical exposure.
outputs: Approved cardiodynamic plan (SAP appendix or standalone); specifications for the concentration-QTc analysis, assumption checks and categorical tables.
standard: ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1); ICH E14
qc: Independent pharmacometrics and statistics review; plan approved before treatment-unblinded ECG data are analyzed.

deliverable: ECG core-laboratory data transfer and blinded-reading specification
description: Study-specific agreement with the ECG core laboratory: extraction of replicate ECGs at each nominal time, blinded central reading, lead and measurement method, transferred variables (RR, QT, QTcF, QTcB, PR, QRS, heart rate, morphology), keys for matching ECGs to PK samples, and reader-variability checks.
inputs: Protocol ECG schedule; cardiodynamic analysis plan; generic data-transfer specification; core-laboratory procedures.
outputs: Signed ECG transfer and reading specification; test-transfer results; reconciliation keys for ADEG and the concentration-QTc dataset.
standard: ICH E14; ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1)
qc: Test transfer before the first production transfer; variables, units and keys checked; ECG and PK times reconciled.

deliverable: Renal impairment analysis section
description: Design-specific SAP section: regression of PK parameters (CL/F, AUC, Cmax, unbound values where relevant) on continuous renal function as the primary approach, GMRs versus the control group with CIs, the reduced-design decision rule, dialysis clearance, sensitivity to the renal function equation, and the method for dose recommendations.
inputs: Renal design basis; protocol estimands; renal function equations; exposure-response information.
outputs: SAP renal section; specifications for renal derivations and outputs.
standard: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal…; Guideline on the evaluation of the pharmacokinetics of…
qc: Independent statistician review; primary approach, decision rule and equations checked for ambiguity.

deliverable: EDC raw data extracts and vendor data transfers (data transfer agreement interface)
description: Scheduled EDC extracts plus external vendor transfers (central laboratory, bioanalytical concentrations, ECG core laboratory, IRT randomization) received under transfer agreements that fix file format, frequency, variable layout, units, code lists and merge keys. Statistical programming and biostatistics confirm that each incoming structure supports the planned SDTM mapping and analysis.
inputs: Protocol; eCRF design; SAP; vendor specifications (central laboratory, bioanalytical laboratory, ECG core laboratory); IRT design; data transfer specifications
outputs: Raw extracts and vendor files feeding SDTM mapping; reconciliation keys for PK, laboratory, ECG and randomization data
standard: ICH E6(R3); EMA/INS/GCP/112288/2023; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Transfer-specification conformance check on every load; record counts and checksums reconciled; test transfer before the first production transfer.

deliverable: Biostatistics review of edit checks, data queries and data-review listings
description: Biostatistics and programming review of the edit-check specification and standing cross-form listings so that analysis-critical fields are clean before lock: dosing versus PK sampling times, nominal versus actual times, BLQ flags, randomization versus treatment received, AE coding, laboratory units and ranges, and ECG intervals. Raises queries and analysis-oriented listings beyond the standard data management checks.
inputs: Raw EDC extracts; edit-check specification; SAP analysis needs; PK analysis plan time-window rules
outputs: Queries on analysis-critical fields; review listings feeding blinded data review and data cleaning
standard: ICH E6(R3)
qc: Independent review of listing logic; queries tracked to closure; critical variables reconciled against the SAP list.

deliverable: Annotated CRF (aCRF), final submission version
description: The blank CRF annotated with SDTM domain and variable names and controlled-terminology mappings, showing the source of every collected SDTM variable. Submitted as acrf.pdf; it is the human-readable companion to the SDTM define.xml and the cSDRG.
inputs: Final blank eCRF; SDTM mapping specification; SDTMIG; controlled terminology
outputs: acrf.pdf for the submission package (eCTD Module 5); page references for define.xml origins and the cSDRG
standard: Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…; Define-XML v2.1; SDTMIG v3.4
qc: Page-by-page review against the final CRF and SDTM specifications; check that every annotated origin resolves in define.xml.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: DM (Demographics)
description: Participant-level demographics tabulation: age, sex, race, ethnicity, country, planned and actual arm, and reference dates (RFSTDTC, RFENDTC). Anchors participant-level traceability and supplemental qualifiers.
inputs: Raw EDC demographics; IRT randomization data; SDTM mapping specification; aCRF
outputs: Source for ADSL and all ADaM datasets; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; reconciliation to raw data and to the randomization schedule.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: PC (Pharmacokinetic Concentrations)
description: Drug and metabolite concentration findings: analyte, result and units, LLOQ and BLQ indicators, specimen, nominal time point and actual collection date and time. It must align with EX dosing records and reconcile to the bioanalytical transfer.
inputs: Bioanalytical concentration transfer; sampling-time CRF data; LLOQ and BLQ conventions from the PK analysis plan; SDTM mapping specification
outputs: Source for ADPC and NCA; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; every record reconciled to the bioanalytical transfer (record count, value, BLQ flag); nominal versus actual time check.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: PP (Pharmacokinetic Parameters)
description: Tabulation of NCA parameters (for example Cmax, Tmax, AUClast, AUCinf, t1/2, CL/F, Vz/F) with PPTESTCD and results, linked to the contributing PC records through RELREC. Values come from the validated NCA run of record, so PP is finalized after NCA.
inputs: NCA output from validated software; PC dataset; parameter list from the PK analysis plan
outputs: Source for ADPP; PK parameter listings; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Reconciliation to the NCA output of record; independent double programming of the SDTM structure; conformance checks.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: EX (Exposure)
description: Actual study drug administration: treatment, dose, units, route, frequency, and start and end date and time of each administration. Critical for multiple-dose accumulation and PK time after dose; it must reconcile to randomization and to PC sampling.
inputs: Dosing CRF; IRT randomization data; SDTM mapping specification; aCRF
outputs: Source for ADSL treatment variables, ADPC time after dose and exposure tables; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; reconciliation to randomization and to PC time-after-dose derivations.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: AE (Adverse Events)
description: Adverse events with MedDRA coding (LLT, PT, SOC), seriousness, severity or grade, causality, onset and resolution, action taken and outcome, plus the dates needed to derive treatment emergence. The core safety tabulation behind dose-escalation decisions.
inputs: AE CRF; MedDRA-coded terms; dosing records for treatment-emergent timing; SDTM mapping specification
outputs: Source for ADAE, safety tables and safety review committee data; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; MedDRA Version 29.1; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; MedDRA coding QC; reconciliation of serious adverse events with the safety database.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: LB (Laboratory)
description: Central and local laboratory findings: test, original and standardized results and units, reference ranges, normal-range indicators, fasting status and baseline flag. Safety laboratories (liver, renal, hematology) are central to Phase 1 monitoring.
inputs: Central laboratory transfer; local laboratory CRF; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Source for ADLB and laboratory safety tables; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; every record reconciled to the laboratory transfer; unit-conversion QC.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: VS (Vital Signs)
description: Vital signs findings (blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, weight, height, BMI) with position and nominal time points relative to dosing, for early-phase hemodynamic safety.
inputs: Vital signs CRF; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Source for ADVS and vital signs tables; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; reconciliation to raw data.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: EG (ECG)
description: ECG findings, including RR, PR, QRS, QT and corrected QT (QTcF, QTcB) intervals and interpretation, with nominal time points aligned to PK sampling where a concentration-QTc analysis is planned.
inputs: ECG core laboratory transfer or ECG CRF; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Source for ADEG and concentration-QTc analysis; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E14
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; reconciliation to the ECG core laboratory transfer; QC of time matching to PK samples.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: DS (Disposition)
description: Participant disposition events and protocol milestones: informed consent, randomization, completion or discontinuation with reason, and epoch transitions. Drives analysis-set derivation and the disposition table.
inputs: Disposition and completion CRF; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Source for ADSL disposition and population flags and for the disposition table; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; reconciliation to enrollment and randomization counts.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: MH (Medical History)
description: Medical and surgical history with MedDRA coding and timing relative to the study; supports eligibility review, baseline characterization and special-population studies.
inputs: Medical history CRF; MedDRA coding; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Baseline characterization in ADSL and listings; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; MedDRA Version 29.1
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; coding QC.

deliverable: SDTM dataset: CM (Concomitant and Prior Medications)
description: Prior and concomitant medications with WHODrug coding (including ATC classes), indication, dose and timing; supports DDI interpretation and checks of protocol-permitted medications.
inputs: Concomitant medication CRF; WHODrug coding; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Concomitant medication listings; DDI context; submission tabulation dataset
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; WHODrug Global (UMCDD)
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; coding QC.

deliverable: SDTM datasets: pharmacodynamic findings, DV and other supporting domains (PE, SU, QS, CO, trial design, SUPPQUAL, RELREC)
description: Pharmacodynamic and biomarker findings in the SDTMIG domain that fits each measurement (for example LB), protocol deviations (DV), physical examination (PE), substance use (SU), questionnaires (QS), comments (CO), special-purpose and trial design domains (SE, SV, TA, TE, TV, TS, TI), and SUPPQUAL and RELREC records.
inputs: CRF and vendor data for each domain; classified deviation log; trial design metadata from the protocol; SDTM mapping specification; controlled terminology
outputs: Source for ADPD and supporting listings; deviation data for analysis-set decisions; trial design metadata for define.xml; submission tabulation datasets
standard: SDTMIG v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; RELREC integrity checks; DV reconciled to the classified deviation log.

deliverable: SDTM Define-XML (define.xml and stylesheet)
description: Machine-readable metadata for every SDTM dataset: dataset, variable and value-level metadata, codelists, computational methods and origins, with links to aCRF pages and the cSDRG. A required component of the tabulation package.
inputs: Final SDTM datasets; SDTM mapping specification; aCRF; controlled terminology; value-level metadata specification
outputs: SDTM define.xml for the submission package (eCTD Module 5); input to conformance checks
standard: Define-XML v2.1; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Define-XML conformance check and dataset-to-define consistency check; peer review; check that origins resolve to aCRF pages.

deliverable: SDTM reviewer guide (cSDRG)
description: Clinical Study Data Reviewer's Guide: orients a regulatory reviewer to the tabulation package (study design, dataset inventory, mapping conventions, sponsor decisions, known data issues) and explains each conformance finding that was not fixed.
inputs: SDTM datasets; SDTM define.xml; conformance report; SDTM mapping specification; protocol
outputs: cSDRG for the submission package (eCTD Module 5)
standard: PHUSE cSDRG Package; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…
qc: Peer review; consistency with define.xml and the conformance explanations; sign-off.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis Dataset)
description: One record per participant with analysis-set flags (for example SAFFL and PK population flags), planned and actual treatment variables (TRTxxP, TRTxxA), demographics, baseline covariates and key dates. The spine merged into every other ADaM dataset.
inputs: SDTM DM, EX and DS; randomization data; SAP analysis-set definitions; ADSL specification
outputs: Merged into all ADaM datasets; population counts for every table; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; population flags reconciled to disposition, randomization and deviation decisions.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADPC (PK concentrations analysis)
description: Analysis-ready concentration dataset with nominal and actual times relative to first dose and to the reference dose, BLQ handling per the analysis rules, and analysis flags such as inclusion in NCA. Direct input to NCA and to concentration tables and figures.
inputs: SDTM PC and EX; ADSL; PK analysis plan (BLQ, time-window and exclusion rules); ADPC specification
outputs: NCA input; concentration tables and figures; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADNCA v1.0; ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; QC of time after dose and BLQ rules; reconciliation to PC.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADPP (PK parameters analysis)
description: Analysis-ready PK parameters from the validated NCA run, with analysis flags, dose-normalized values and the grouping needed for dose-proportionality, accumulation, food-effect, DDI and BA or BE analyses.
inputs: SDTM PP; ADSL; ADPC; PK analysis plan; ADPP specification
outputs: PK parameter tables; inputs to ANOVA and geometric mean ratio analyses; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; CDISC Controlled Terminology
qc: Reconciliation to the NCA output of record; independent double programming; conformance checks.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADAE (adverse events analysis)
description: Analysis-ready AE dataset in the occurrence data structure with the treatment-emergent flag (TRTEMFL), severity and causality analysis variables, treatment period and first-occurrence flags. Drives all TEAE tables and dose-escalation safety review.
inputs: SDTM AE and EX; ADSL; SAP TEAE definition; ADAE specification
outputs: TEAE, SAE and severity tables; safety review committee data; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaM OCCDS v1.1; MedDRA Version 29.1
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; QC of TRTEMFL logic; reconciliation to SDTM AE and the safety database.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADLB (laboratory analysis)
description: Analysis-ready laboratory data (BDS): baseline and change from baseline, standardized results, shift and toxicity-grade categories, and analysis flags. Central to Phase 1 safety laboratory monitoring, including the components of a Hy's law evaluation.
inputs: SDTM LB; ADSL; SAP baseline, shift and grading rules; ADLB specification
outputs: Laboratory tables (summary, shift, change, marked abnormality); submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; CTCAE v6.0 (MedDRA 28.0)
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; QC of baseline, change and category derivations; reconciliation to LB.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADVS (vital signs analysis)
description: Analysis-ready vital signs (BDS) with baseline, change from baseline, position handling and analysis flags for hemodynamic safety summaries.
inputs: SDTM VS; ADSL; SAP rules; ADVS specification
outputs: Vital signs tables; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaMIG v1.3
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; baseline and change QC; reconciliation to VS.

deliverable: ADaM dataset: ADEG (ECG analysis)
description: Analysis-ready ECG data (BDS) with QTc baseline and change from baseline, categorical outlier flags, and concentrations time-matched from ADPC for concentration-QTc analysis.
inputs: SDTM EG; ADPC (time-matched concentrations); ADSL; SAP QTc rules; ADEG specification
outputs: QTc tables and outlier summaries; concentration-QTc analysis input; submission analysis dataset
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; ICH E14; ICH E14/S7B Q&As (R1)
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; QC of QTc categories and time matching; reconciliation to EG.

deliverable: ADaM datasets: ADPD and other analysis datasets (ADCM, ADMH, deviation or exposure analysis datasets as applicable)
description: Pharmacodynamic and biomarker analysis dataset (BDS) with baseline, change and PK-PD linkage, plus other SAP-specified analysis datasets, for example ADCM, ADMH, exposure, deviation or immunogenicity datasets.
inputs: SDTM pharmacodynamic, biomarker, CM, MH and other source domains; ADSL; ADPC or ADPP for PK-PD linkage; SAP; ADaM specifications
outputs: PD tables and figures; exposure-response and modeling inputs; supporting tables; submission analysis datasets
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; ADaM OCCDS v1.1
qc: Independent double programming and conformance checks; QC of PK-PD linkage and of baseline and change derivations.

deliverable: ADaM Define-XML (define.xml and stylesheet)
description: Machine-readable metadata for the ADaM package: dataset, variable and value-level metadata, codelists, derivation methods and traceability to SDTM sources. A required component of the analysis package.
inputs: Final ADaM datasets; ADaM specifications; derivation methods; controlled terminology; SDTM source references
outputs: ADaM define.xml for the submission package (eCTD Module 5); input to conformance checks
standard: Define-XML v2.1; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…
qc: Define-XML conformance and dataset-to-define consistency checks; review of derivation methods; traceability check.

deliverable: ADaM reviewer guide (ADRG)
description: Analysis Data Reviewer's Guide: orients reviewers to the analysis package, including analysis-set derivations, key derivations and conventions, conformance findings and their explanations, SDTM-to-ADaM traceability, and links to the SAP and outputs.
inputs: ADaM datasets; ADaM define.xml; conformance report; SAP; analysis-set definitions; traceability matrix
outputs: ADRG for the submission package (eCTD Module 5)
standard: PHUSE ADRG Package; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…
qc: Peer review; consistency with define.xml, the SAP and the conformance explanations; sign-off.

deliverable: CDISC conformance report: SDTM, ADaM and Define-XML
description: Conformance validation of the SDTM and ADaM datasets and both define.xml files against the applicable CDISC and FDA rules, with every finding triaged: fixed in the data or metadata, or explained in the reviewer guides. The gate for package readiness.
inputs: SDTM and ADaM datasets; define.xml files; controlled terminology version; validation rule set and version
outputs: Issue list with dispositions; explanations for the cSDRG and ADRG; package go or no-go
standard: FDA Validator Rules v1.6; SDTM and SDTMIG Conformance Rules v2.0; ADaM Conformance Rules v5.0; Study Data Technical Conformance Guide: Technical…
qc: Validator and rule-set versions recorded; every finding dispositioned; explanations reconciled with the reviewer guides.

deliverable: PK bioanalytical sample reconciliation (concentration data load and BLQ handling)
description: Reconciles the bioanalytical concentration transfer against the clinical sampling record: every collected sample accounted for (analyzed, missing, insufficient, reassayed), LLOQ and BLQ flags consistent with the analysis plan, analyte and units mapped correctly, and collection times verified. The gate for loading concentrations into PC.
inputs: Bioanalytical transfer from the validated assay; PK sampling CRF; LLOQ and BLQ rules; sample accountability log
outputs: Reconciled concentration load; documented BLQ handling; resolved discrepancies
standard: ICH M10; SDTMIG v3.4; 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Every sample accounted for; independent check of BLQ and LLOQ flags; record counts and values matched to the transfer.

deliverable: Blinded data review outputs (data-review listings and review meeting package)
description: Pre-lock listings and summaries (data quality, candidate protocol deviations, outliers, missing data, PK time-window issues) prepared for the data review meeting where analysis-set assignments and deviation classifications are agreed before unblinding. In blinded studies the package carries no treatment information.
inputs: Cleaned, blinded SDTM or raw data; data review plan; SAP analysis-set and deviation rules
outputs: Meeting package; proposed analysis-set and deviation classifications; inputs to soft and hard lock
standard: ICH E9
qc: Independent review of listing logic; decisions minuted before unblinding; reconciliation to SAP rules.

deliverable: Dry-run datasets and dry-run TLF execution
description: End-to-end run of the SDTM, ADaM and TLF programs on a pre-lock or dummy data cut to test the pipeline, the shells and program robustness before lock; surfaces specification and program defects early.
inputs: Interim or dummy data cut; ADaM specifications; TLF shells; programs under development
outputs: Defect list for specifications and programs; confirmation that production can run at lock
standard: ICH E9
qc: Independent programming on the dry run where planned; output-versus-shell reconciliation; defects tracked to closure.

deliverable: Data cleaning and soft lock
description: Interim freeze once queries are resolved or dispositioned, coding is complete, reconciliations (serious adverse events, PK samples, laboratory, randomization) are closed and data review decisions are captured, allowing final checks before hard lock. Signed off.
inputs: Query status; coding status; reconciliation status; data review decisions
outputs: Soft-locked snapshot for final checks; readiness for hard lock; sign-off record
standard: ICH E6(R3); 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Lock checklist completed; cross-functional reconciliation sign-off; audit-trail review.

deliverable: Database hard lock
description: Formal lock: data frozen, write access removed and a final snapshot taken under change control. The stage 3 exit gate and the data freeze on which final datasets and reported outputs are based.
inputs: Soft-lock status; closed reconciliations; final coding; data review decisions; lock authorization
outputs: Locked database snapshot; final SDTM and ADaM regeneration; unblinding can proceed
standard: ICH E6(R3); 21 CFR Part 11
qc: Hard-lock checklist with multi-party sign-off; verification that write access is removed; snapshot integrity check.

deliverable: Traceability matrix: raw data to SDTM to ADaM
description: End-to-end matrix linking CRF and raw sources to SDTM variables (through the aCRF and define.xml), SDTM to ADaM derivations (through define.xml and the ADRG), and ADaM to analysis outputs, showing an unbroken chain for inspection and submission.
inputs: aCRF; SDTM and ADaM define.xml; mapping and derivation specifications; reviewer guides
outputs: Traceability evidence for submission and inspection; input to the ADRG and CSR appendices
standard: ADaMIG v1.3; Define-XML v2.1
qc: Cross-link verification from raw to SDTM to ADaM; peer review; consistency with define.xml and the reviewer guides.

deliverable: Controlled terminology and coding-dictionary version management (CDISC CT, MedDRA, WHODrug)
description: Documented record of the CDISC CT, MedDRA and WHODrug versions used, with an impact assessment if recoding occurs, keeping SDTM, ADaM and define.xml consistent and coding reproducible.
inputs: Dictionary versions; coding decisions; CT subsets used in mapping
outputs: Version records for define.xml and the reviewer guides; reproducible coding
standard: CDISC Controlled Terminology; MedDRA Version 29.1; WHODrug Global (UMCDD); Define-XML v2.1
qc: Version-lock verification; CT conformance checks; coding QC against the locked dictionaries.

deliverable: Randomization QC and verification report (schedule versus IRT and EDC reconciliation)
